name: UT-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a 17-point partisan lean
Incumbent Mike Kennedy has a large fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 95%
Democratic challenger has raised minimal funds
model.rationale: The district's 17-point Republican lean, Kennedy's overwhelming financial edge, and markets pricing him near 95% all point to a safe Republican hold. No polls or expert ratings suggest any meaningful challenge.
model.watch: A major outside-spending surge for Larsen or a dramatic shift in the national environment could make this competitive, but nothing in the current evidence suggests that.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Utah's 4th District is a solidly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about 17 points toward the GOP. Incumbent Mike Kennedy is running for reelection and holds a commanding financial advantage, having raised roughly $970,000 with nearly $390,000 on hand. His Democratic challenger, Jonny Larsen, has raised about $54,000 and had just over $1,100 in cash as of the latest filings.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets give the Republican about a 95% chance of winning. An independent and a Libertarian are also on the ballot but have raised little. The district's lean, the incumbent's resources, and market pricing all point to a comfortable Republican victory in November.
